Escalation check per SHARED-FINDINGS section 2: this unit's C# body loops `base.Creature.CombatState.GetOpponentsOf(base.Creature)` (Aeonglass.cs:78-83), i.e. it DOES read the combat's creature lists at add-to-room time -- but it reads the OPPONENT side (the player), which exists before create_monsters runs, not `hooks.combat.enemies`, which does not (combat.py:134). In Ironclad scope that loop has exactly one iteration, so the sim's single unconditional application is equivalent; the per-opponent instancing half is audit/records/power/withering_presence.json's InstanceType gap. Application ORDER (WitheringPresence then Artifact) matches Aeonglass.cs:78-84. The `NRunMusicController.UpdateMusicParameter("queen_progress", 1f)` at :77 is presentation.

AfterCardGeneratedForCombat.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 8.) IMPLEMENTED, not merely proven dormant-safe. monsters/glory/aeonglass.py gained `_AeonglassWitherListener` (the queen.py `_AmalgamDeathListener` pattern for the missing MonsterModel listener category, hook_dispatch/G5), registered in Aeonglass.__init__; its on_card_generated_for_combat mirrors Aeonglass.cs:150-166 exactly, including post-increment ordering. Both open-coded upgrade loops deleted (the boss's own Increasing-Intensity add and WitheringPresencePower's punish-Wither add); TDD proves exact equivalence for both former sites. The record's own anticipated trigger -- 'any third Wither source -- drawing one from StatusCardPool.cs:28' -- turned out to be ALREADY REACHABLE: `wither` sits in transform_options_in_combat's Status pool, so an Entropy transform could roll one; before this task such a Wither was silently un-upgraded (the old 'NOT LIVE, executed' dormancy verdict was stale). Root cause of the stale verdict: audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py's probe_wither() greps literally for 'WitherCard(' and cannot see make_card()-style dynamic construction -- a probe blind spot reported in GAP-QUEUE.md's Outstanding record defects. With step61's dispatch wired, a transform-rolled Wither now arrives fake-upgraded (test_task8_aeonglass_generated_wither.py, 7 tests). NOT closed: the six other C# AfterCardGeneratedForCombat implementers (Regalite, RocketPunch, ArsenalPower, PillarOfCreationPower, SmokestackPower, TrashToTreasurePower) remain unported. power/withering_presence's ExtraHoverTips citation stays a reported-not-edited inconsistency.  The text it replaced read: THE SECOND OF THIS UNIT'S TWO UNCLAIMED C# HOOK OVERRIDES, and unlike AfterDeath it is genuinely mechanical -- read to the end and it is still mechanical. Aeonglass.cs:150-166: for EVERY card generated for combat, if it is a Wither, call `MatchWitherToUpgradeCount(wither)`, which applies `wither.FakeUpgrade()` WitherUpgradeCount times. The hook is dispatched by Hook.AfterCardGeneratedForCombat from CardPileCmd.cs:246 (inside AddGeneratedCardsToCombat, per generated card) and CardCmd.cs:504, i.e. it is a GENERAL interception point that catches Withers from any source. The sim has no such dispatch and no MonsterModel listener category (hook_dispatch G5, not re-verdicted), so the effect is open-coded at each of the sim's two Wither-creating sites instead: aeonglass.py:78-82 fake-upgrades the boss's own new Wither, and powers.py:3284-3289 (WitheringPresencePower) fake-upgrades the punish Wither by reading `getattr(self.owner, "wither_upgrade_count", 0)`. Note that the C# line the power record cites for the same behaviour, WitheringPresencePower.cs:37, is inside `ExtraHoverTips` -- a HOVER-TIP preview property -- not inside AfterCardPlayed; the real Wither the power adds at :55 is matched only via this Aeonglass hook, so the sim's open-coding is standing in for THIS override at both sites, not for that line. **NOT LIVE, executed** (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py wither`): the sim constructs a WitherCard at exactly two sites, aeonglass.py:79 and powers.py:3286, and both already apply the upgrade count, so no ported path can produce an unmatched Wither today. Named triggers that would make it live: (a) porting anything that draws Wither from the status pool -- StatusCardPool.cs:28 lists Wither among its 12 entries, so any 'add a random status' card/relic/potion reaches it; (b) a second monster or power adding Wither during an Aeonglass fight; (c) porting Regalite, RocketPunch, ArsenalPower, PillarOfCreationPower, SmokestackPower or TrashToTreasurePower, the other six AfterCardGeneratedForCombat implementers, which would need the dispatch to exist at all.

guards.what: Wither pile position is BOTTOM, not Random
guards.rationale: Checked because the sibling finding on the_insatiable is a live gap. Aeonglass.cs:145 is `AddToCombatAndPreview<Wither>(targets, PileType.Discard, WitherAmount, null)` and omits the `position` argument, so it takes the default `CardPilePosition.Bottom` (CardPileCmd.cs:997, :1005) -- which resolves to index -1 (CardPileCmd.cs:512) and draws no RNG. aeonglass.py:82 uses `CardPileCmd.add_to_discard`, an append (cmds.py:464-472). Same position, same zero draws. This is exactly the helper the_insatiable should NOT have used, and here it is the right one.

guards.what: Increasing Intensity: existing Withers upgraded, then the counter, then the new card
guards.rationale: C# order (Aeonglass.cs:130-147): FakeUpgrade every existing Wither in `target.Player.PlayerCombatState.AllCards`; `WitherUpgradeCount++`; add the new Wither, which the AfterCardGeneratedForCombat hook then upgrades to the NEW count; apply Strength; `AdditionalStrength++`. Sim order (aeonglass.py:74-87): upgrade existing; increment the counter; build the WitherCard and fake-upgrade it to the new count; add it; Strength; increment. The one difference is that the sim upgrades the new card BEFORE it enters the pile and the game upgrades it AFTER, i.e. C# fires the pile-entry path on an un-upgraded card. Same observable: the sim's only pile-entry work is `CardPileCmd._enter_combat` (cmds.py:472), and no ported listener reads a card's upgrade level at that moment. Named trigger: any listener on card-entering-combat that branches on upgrade level.

C# `PlayerCombatState.AllCards` is `AllPiles.SelectMany(...)` over FIVE piles -- Hand, DrawPile, DiscardPile, ExhaustPile and **PlayPile** (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-82). The sim's `all_cards` is hand + draw + discard + exhaust (player.py:100-103) and its docstring claims it mirrors AllCards, which is inaccurate. Not a divergence at this site, argued rather than assumed: Increasing Intensity is a MONSTER move and runs during the enemy side, when no player card is mid-play, so the play pile is empty and the two sets coincide. Flagged so a later reader does not inherit the docstring (PROMPT.md class 24 shape, in player.py rather than in this unit).
